analyst_view.overall: This is Tenerife's first match since striker Jesús de Miguel died on 3 November, a day after colliding with Andorra's goalkeeper at the Heliodoro; their game at Granada was postponed, so the emotional context outweighs anything in the numbers. Álvaro Cervera's side had drawn four in a row before that, while bottom club Ceuta (five points, 30 goals conceded) lost 3-0 at Córdoba last time out and, per one earlier report, have a new coach in Sergio Lobera. I found little fresh team news for this match this week, and no referee had been named when this was written.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.5 goals and I stay there. Ceuta concede more than two a game, which points up, but Tenerife have been a draw team and have scored only 15 in 12 games. An emotionally heavy day is hard to read either way.

corners.text: The numbers say 8.7 corners and I leave it. Tenerife should have more of the territory against a side that has lost five in a row, but the site already gives them the larger share, and Ceuta are likely to try to stay compact.

cards.text: The numbers say 5.7 cards. I lean lower: in the first game at the Heliodoro since De Miguel's death, I expect both teams to avoid flashpoints, and Tenerife are among the cleaner sides (28 yellows in 12 games by LaLiga's count). Ceuta's 35 yellows are the main risk to this lean.

shots.text: The numbers say 23.7 shots. I have changed my lean from higher to lower: LaLiga counts Tenerife at only 94 shots in 12 games, the lowest rate of any team I checked this round, so even against the league's worst defence their 11.9 looks high. Ceuta shoot more (142 in 13) but have scored only ten goals.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 7.6 shots on target. I have moved from higher to same: Ceuta's defence has been breached 30 times and Enric Gallego has eight goals, but Tenerife's low shot volume holds me back from going higher.
